To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) CD44 splice variants are expressed in activated T cells, in non-HL, and in colorectral cancer; and 2) expression of variant CD4 is related to tumor progression in non-HL and colorectal cancer.

CD44 variant expression is upregulated in activated T lymphocytes, in aggressive lymphoma and in colorectal cancer, and that the variant expressed in lymphocytes and aggressive lymphomas is the same that confers metastatic potential to rat tumor cell lines.

variant CD44 glycoforms are overexpressed in non-Hodkin's lymphoma and colorectal cancer, that the expression is related to the grade of malignancy and to areas of dyspasia in adenomatous tissue, that the overexpression in non-Hodgin's lymphoma is associated with the aggressive phenotype, and that the variant CD44 glycopeptides contain the v6 exon, a domain that in the rat is part of the metastasis conferring variant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of a recently described variant of CD44 in human lymphohematopoiesis and in tumor progression.
the expression of CD44 splice variant proteins in human lymphohematopoiesis and in human tumors.

the expression of CD44 splice variant glycoprotein during lymphocyte activation as well as during the development of lymphoid tumors and colorectal carcinomas, with the aim to elucidate the biological role of the CD44 variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the variant form of CD44 is not only a marker of metastatic potential, but is also a marker of tumor progression.
CD44 splice variants are not only expressed in tumor cells but are also overexpressed during lymphocyte activation.
the expression of CD44 variants is associated with lymphocyte activation and with tumor progression in lymphomas and colorectal carcinomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD44 variants are upregulated during tumor progression, and that this upregulation is a marker of tumor aggressiveness.
the variant CD44 splice forms are expressed at low levels in normal lymphoid tissue, and that they are upregulated upon lymphocyte activation.
variant CD44 glycoconjugates are expressed on activated lymphocytes, in aggressive NHL, and in colorectral cancer, suggesting a role of variant CD44 molecules in the progression of these diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

variant CD44 glycoconjugates are upregulated in activated human T lymphocytes, in several non-Hodgkins lymphomas, and, in colorectal cancer, in adenoma, in invasive carcinoma, and in carcinoma metastasis.
the variant CD44 glycoforms, which are not expressed in resting cells, are upregulated upon activation and during tumor progression.
the expression of the v6 variant is upregulated in aggressive lymphomas, and is a tumor progression marker for colorectal cancer.
